items.q: Lan: Where's Nam? / Minh: He ______ for a job interview at the moment, so don't disturb him.
items.vi: Lan: Nam đâu rồi? / Minh: Bạn ấy đang chuẩn bị cho buổi phỏng vấn xin việc lúc này, nên đừng làm phiền.
items.explanation: At the moment signals an action happening right now, so the present continuous is preparing is needed; the simple present, present perfect and past do not describe an ongoing action at the time of speaking.

items.q: Our garden party was cancelled because of a sudden ______ that flooded the lawn in minutes.
items.vi: Bữa tiệc ngoài vườn của chúng tôi bị hủy vì một trận mưa như trút bất ngờ làm ngập bãi cỏ chỉ trong vài phút.
items.explanation: A downpour is a sudden, very heavy fall of rain — the only option that could flood a lawn in minutes. Drizzle is very light rain, mist is thin fog, and frost is ice on cold surfaces.

items.q: My brother has to ______ a decision about which career to follow before he finishes school.
items.vi: Anh trai tôi phải đưa ra quyết định về nghề nghiệp sẽ theo đuổi trước khi học xong.
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is make a decision. Do, have and get do not combine with decision in this meaning.

items.q: Nam: Should I take the job in Da Nang or stay here? / Lan: ______ is that you need a steady income, so take it.
items.vi: Nam: Mình nên nhận việc ở Đà Nẵng hay ở lại đây? / Lan: Điều cốt lõi là cậu cần một nguồn thu nhập ổn định, nên nhận đi.
items.explanation: The bottom line means the most important fact that decides a matter. The last straw is the final problem that makes you lose patience, the tip of the iceberg is a small visible part of a bigger problem, and the eleventh hour is the last possible moment.

items.q: Lan: Why isn't Minh at school anymore? / Nam: He decided to ______ of school to help his father at the shop.
items.vi: Lan: Sao Minh không còn đi học nữa? / Nam: Cậu ấy quyết định bỏ học để phụ bố ở cửa hàng.
items.explanation: Drop out of school means to leave before finishing. Drop off means to fall asleep or deliver someone, while drop in and drop by mean to pay a short visit — none takes of school.

items.q: You ______ such an expensive present; just coming to my birthday party was enough.
items.vi: Bạn không cần phải mua món quà đắt tiền như vậy đâu; chỉ cần đến dự sinh nhật mình là đủ rồi.
items.explanation: Needn't have + past participle says that something was done but was not necessary. Can't have expresses a past deduction, won't have is future perfect, and mustn't have is not used for a past action that was unnecessary.

items.q: Do you remember the year ______ our family first moved to Ho Chi Minh City?
items.vi: Bạn có nhớ năm mà gia đình chúng ta lần đầu chuyển đến Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh không?
items.explanation: When is the relative adverb for a time noun such as the year. Where refers to a place, whom to a person, and which would need a preposition (in which) to follow the year.

items.q: Dad drove to work very slowly because of the thick ______ on the road this morning.
items.vi: Sáng nay bố lái xe đi làm rất chậm vì sương mù dày đặc trên đường.
items.explanation: Thick fog makes it hard to see, so drivers slow down. Hail is frozen rain, thunder is the sound of a storm, and drought is a long period without rain — none is described as thick on the road.

items.q: By the time we got to Hoa's house, the party ______.
items.vi: Lúc chúng tôi đến nhà Hoa thì bữa tiệc đã bắt đầu rồi.
items.explanation: By the time + past simple describes an action that was completed before another past action, so the past perfect had already started is required.

items.q: There isn't ______ milk left in the fridge, so could you buy some on the way home?
items.vi: Trong tủ lạnh không còn nhiều sữa, nên bạn mua thêm trên đường về nhà được không?
items.explanation: Milk is uncountable, so it takes much in a negative sentence. Many, a few and few are only used with plural countable nouns.

items.q: Put on your coat, or you will ______ a cold waiting for the bus in this wind.
items.vi: Mặc áo khoác vào đi, không thì bạn sẽ bị cảm lạnh khi đứng đợi xe buýt trong gió này.
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is catch a cold (become ill with one). Take, hold and bring do not combine with a cold in this meaning.

items.q: My aunt is used to ______ up early because she runs a stall at the market.
items.vi: Dì tôi đã quen với việc dậy sớm vì dì bán hàng ở chợ.
items.explanation: Be used to (= be accustomed to) is followed by a noun or a gerund: used to getting up. The to-infinitive (used to get up) only follows used to without be, when it describes a past habit.

items.q: My uncle's farm lost most of its rice this year because of the long ______.
items.vi: Nông trại của chú tôi mất gần hết lúa năm nay vì đợt hạn hán kéo dài.
items.explanation: A drought is a long period with no rain, which dries up crops, and it is the only option naturally described as long. A flood is too much water, while hail and lightning are short events in a storm.

items.q: Nam wants to become a doctor, ______ his twin brother dreams of opening a restaurant.
items.vi: Nam muốn trở thành bác sĩ, trong khi người anh sinh đôi của cậu ấy lại mơ mở một nhà hàng.
items.explanation: Whereas is a conjunction that contrasts two clauses in one sentence. However needs a full stop or semicolon before it, therefore shows a result, and so that shows purpose.

items.q: Could you ______ my little sister from school today? I have a job interview at three.
items.vi: Hôm nay bạn đón em gái mình ở trường giúp được không? Mình có buổi phỏng vấn xin việc lúc ba giờ.
items.explanation: Pick up someone from a place means to collect them. Drop off is the opposite (leave someone at a place), take up means start a hobby, and bring up means raise a child or mention a topic.

items.q: If I ______ you, I would apply for the job at the new hotel before somebody else does.
items.vi: Nếu tôi là bạn, tôi sẽ nộp đơn xin việc ở khách sạn mới trước khi người khác nộp.
items.explanation: The second conditional gives advice about an unreal present situation: If I were you, I would.... Am and will be belong to the first conditional, and had been would need would have applied.

items.q: Lan: I want to save up for a new laptop. / Nam: Then you'll have to ______ and stop buying bubble tea every day.
items.vi: Lan: Mình muốn để dành tiền mua laptop mới. / Nam: Vậy thì cậu phải thắt lưng buộc bụng và ngừng mua trà sữa mỗi ngày.
items.explanation: Tighten your belt means to spend less money because you have less of it. Hold your horses means wait, keep your chin up means stay cheerful, and bite your tongue means stop yourself from speaking.

items.q: The invitations for the party ______ to all our classmates yesterday.
items.vi: Thiệp mời dự tiệc đã được gửi tới tất cả các bạn cùng lớp hôm qua.
items.explanation: The invitations receive the action, so the passive is needed, and yesterday fixes the past simple: were sent. Have been sent cannot go with a finished past time, and sent alone is active.

items.q: After the rain stopped, a bright ______ stretched across the sky above our house.
items.vi: Sau khi mưa tạnh, một chiếc cầu vồng rực rỡ trải dài trên bầu trời phía trên nhà chúng tôi.
items.explanation: A rainbow is the coloured arc that appears in the sky after rain. Thunder is a sound, lightning is a sudden flash during a storm, and hail is frozen rain — none stretches across the sky after the rain has stopped.

items.q: Mai said that she ______ her grandparents in the countryside the following weekend.
items.vi: Mai nói rằng cô ấy sẽ về thăm ông bà ở quê vào cuối tuần sau đó.
items.explanation: After a past reporting verb (said), will shifts back to would, and the following weekend confirms reported speech. The other options keep a present tense that does not match said.

items.q: My cousins are going to ______ a party for Grandma's seventieth birthday next month.
items.vi: Các anh chị họ của tôi sẽ tổ chức một bữa tiệc mừng sinh nhật lần thứ bảy mươi của bà vào tháng sau.
items.explanation: In English you throw (or have/hold) a party. Make a party, do a party and put a party are not English collocations.

items.q: My father ______ at the same bank since he left college, and he still enjoys it.
items.vi: Bố tôi đã làm việc ở cùng một ngân hàng kể từ khi rời trường cao đẳng, và bố vẫn thích công việc đó.
items.explanation: Since + a past starting point with a situation that continues to now takes the present perfect: has worked. The simple present, present continuous and past simple do not link a past start to the present.

items.q: At the class reunion, I finally had time to catch up ______ my old friends.
items.vi: Ở buổi họp lớp, cuối cùng tôi cũng có thời gian hàn huyên với bạn bè cũ.
items.explanation: Catch up with someone means to talk to them and find out their news. Catch up on is used with things you missed (work, sleep), and to and at do not follow catch up.

items.q: Check the weather ______ before you invite everyone to the beach on Sunday.
items.vi: Hãy xem dự báo thời tiết trước khi mời mọi người đi biển vào Chủ nhật.
items.explanation: A weather forecast is a prediction of the coming weather, which is what you check before planning a trip. Climate is the usual weather of a region over years, temperature is only how hot or cold it is, and season is a part of the year.

items.q: Living in the city is ______ more expensive than living in our hometown, so I might move back after graduation.
items.vi: Sống ở thành phố đắt đỏ hơn nhiều so với sống ở quê, nên có lẽ tôi sẽ chuyển về sau khi tốt nghiệp.
items.explanation: A comparative (more expensive) can be strengthened with far, much or a lot. Very, too and so modify plain adjectives, not comparatives.
